chunk_findings.detail: The test claims to verify that `running` and `interrupted` are distinct, but after monkeypatching the clock so both claims are expired it asserts `running == interrupted`. With tasks `A` and `B` claimed and then their leases expired, those items are no longer live-running; they are interrupted. If the implementation follows this test, `ddflow next --state running --json` will return dead/expired claims as the running set, so a lane asking for “running” work will receive items that are actually in the interrupted set and may avoid requeuing or handling them. The expired-lease case should assert that `interrupted` contains `A` and `B` while `running` does not include them (or otherwise excludes interrupted items), not that the two sets are equal.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_next.py:test_state_running_is_distinct_from_interrupted

chunk_findings.detail: The new `--state` handling is not combined with the existing `--lane` handling. `_next` returns the lane answer before reaching the new `if state:` block, while `_next_text` now checks `a.get("state")` before `a.get("lane")`. Given an accepted call such as `ddflow next --lane L --state running` (or MCP `ddflow_next(lane="L", state="running")`), the lane branch drops the state filter, but the text renderer still takes the state branch and calls `_state_text` on a lane answer. The result is that the requested running list for lane `L` is not produced; the flags are silently mishandled unless they are combined or explicitly rejected.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/lifecycle/navigate.py:_next/_next_text

chunk_findings.detail: The test configures `output.max_rows` to 5 and creates 12 blocked items, but it never asserts that the returned `items` list is actually truncated to 5 rows. It only checks metadata (`count`, `truncated.lists.items`, and the next-page cursor) and discards the returned `_items`. Therefore, an implementation of `next --state blocked` that returns all 12 rows while still setting the truncation metadata and cursor would pass this test, despite violating the paging cap that the test is supposed to verify.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_next.py:test_state_is_paged_and_footer_names_the_state

chunk_findings.detail: `_interrupted_rows` can only return interrupted items by filtering `plan.running` for ids that appear in `data["interrupted"]`, which means `plan.running` must contain the interrupted RUNNING items. The `running` builder, however, returns every item in `plan.running` without excluding those interrupted ids. Given an item `task-1` that is RUNNING with no live lease (so `data["interrupted"]` contains `"task-1 is RUNNING..."` and `task-1` is in `plan.running`), `ddflow next --state interrupted` lists `task-1`, but `ddflow next --state running` also lists `task-1`. That violates the intent's "exactly the running or interrupted set" and makes a lane asking for running items see interrupted/stale work as running.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/lifecycle/navigate.py:_STATE_ROW_BUILDER

chunk_findings.detail: When `--state` is used with filters, the answer is filtered by those filters but the paging/footer token is not. `_state_answer(out, state, phase, tags)` receives `phase` and `tags` (and `next_item` receives `kind`, `agent`, `phase_only`), but the token passed to `_cap` is only `_state_token(state)`. `output_caps._entry` then turns that token into `next --state <state>` and pages the `items` list under that token. For example, `ddflow next --state blocked --phase p1` will produce a footer/next call like `ddflow next --state blocked`, dropping `--phase p1`; a subsequent page can therefore come from the unfiltered token and mix blocked items from other phases. The same problem applies to `--tag`, `--kind`, `--agent`, and `--phase-only`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/lifecycle/navigate.py:_state_answer/_state_token

chunk_findings.detail: The new `state` handling cannot honor both `--lane` and `--state`. The lane path calls the lane API without `state`, while the state path calls `_state_answer` without `lane`; there is no call that passes both parameters to the underlying API. However, `_next_text` and `_next_notes` test `a.get("state")` before checking `lane`. Since the `state` Param is independent and has no mutual exclusion with `lane`, a request such as `ddflow next --lane L --state interrupted` (or the equivalent MCP `ddflow_next` call) is inconsistent: either the lane answer is rendered as a state list, or the state answer ignores the requested lane. In either case, the interrupted set for lane `L` is not returned.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/lifecycle/navigate.py:_next_text

chunk_findings.detail: `test_state_interrupted_lists_expired_running_only` asserts that after both leases are expired, `--state running` still lists `{"A", "B"}` while `--state interrupted` also lists them. The intent is to let a lane get “exactly the running or interrupted set” machine-readably, and the earlier test is named `test_state_running_lists_live_claims_not_ready`, so a script using `--state running` as the live-running set will get stale, lease-expired items and may skip work that is actually available/interrupted.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_next.py:79-80

chunk_findings.detail: The state listing does not use a consistent item identifier: `--state ready`, `--state running`, and `--state interrupted` rows are checked using `r["id"]` (lines 37, 56, 77), but `--state blocked` rows are required to have `r["item"]` and the test asserts `all("item" in r ...)`. Given `ddflow --json next --state blocked`, a script that uniformly enumerates ids with `r["id"]` will raise `KeyError: 'id'`, defeating the stated machine-readable listing goal.

chunk_findings.detail: The state next-page token is built from `state`, `kind`, `phase`, and `phase_only`, but the answer being capped is `_state_answer(out, state, phase, tags)`, so `tags` is part of the current state selection while the cursor omits it. Page 2 is therefore recomputed without the `urgent` tag and can return non-urgent blocked items or skip the remaining urgent blocked items.

chunk_findings.detail: `_split_state` parses tags by splitting on `" --tag "` but uses `maxsplit=1` incorrectly for subsequent tags: `rest.split(" --tag ")[1:]` returns only the text *after* the first occurrence of `" --tag "` (split into one element or multiple depending on string structure), which drops any tags that appear before others or truncates the tag extraction when multiple tags are present. For example, given `rest = "running --tag tag1 --tag tag2"`, `rest.split(" --tag ")[1:]` produces `['tag1 --tag tag2']` as a single tuple element instead of `('tag1', 'tag2')`, corrupting the tag reconstruction in the output caps.

chunk_findings.detail: The new tag round-trip treats tag values as bare command-string tokens. `_state_token` appends ` --tag {t}` without quoting, and the MCP next-page argument is built with `t_args.append("tag=" + ",".join(tags))`, then joined into a space-separated command string. Given `ddflow next --state blocked --tag "urgent task" --max-rows 5` and more than five blocked items tagged `urgent task`, the first page is filtered correctly, but the generated MCP next-page command is tokenized as `tag=urgent` plus a stray `task` argument (and a tag containing a comma is likewise split into two tags). The CLI branch quotes each tag with `shlex.quote(t)`, so the two next-page commands are not equivalent for the same tag value; the second page can be filtered by the wrong tag.

chunk_findings.detail: `_interrupted_rows` can only return interrupted items by filtering `plan.running` for ids that appear in `data["interrupted"]`, which means `plan.running` must contain the interrupted RUNNING items. The `running` builder, however, returns every item in `plan.running` without excluding those interrupted ids. Given an item `task-1` that is RUNNING with no live lease (so `data["interrupted"]` contains `"task-1 is RUNNING..."` and `task-1` is in `plan.running`), `ddflow next --state interrupted` lists `task-1`, but `ddflow next --state running` also lists `task-1`. That violates the intent's "exactly the running or interrupted set" and makes a lane asking for running items see interrupted/stale work as running.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/lifecycle/navigate.py:_STATE_ROW_BUILDER

chunk_findings.detail: When `--state` is used with filters, the answer is filtered by those filters but the paging/footer token is not. `_state_answer(out, state, phase, tags)` receives `phase` and `tags` (and `next_item` receives `kind`, `agent`, `phase_only`), but the token passed to `_cap` is only `_state_token(state)`. `output_caps._entry` then turns that token into `next --state <state>` and pages the `items` list under that token. For example, `ddflow next --state blocked --phase p1` will produce a footer/next call like `ddflow next --state blocked`, dropping `--phase p1`; a subsequent page can therefore come from the unfiltered token and mix blocked items from other phases. The same problem applies to `--tag`, `--kind`, `--agent`, and `--phase-only`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/lifecycle/navigate.py:_state_answer/_state_token

chunk_findings.detail: The new `state` handling cannot honor both `--lane` and `--state`. The lane path calls the lane API without `state`, while the state path calls `_state_answer` without `lane`; there is no call that passes both parameters to the underlying API. However, `_next_text` and `_next_notes` test `a.get("state")` before checking `lane`. Since the `state` Param is independent and has no mutual exclusion with `lane`, a request such as `ddflow next --lane L --state interrupted` (or the equivalent MCP `ddflow_next` call) is inconsistent: either the lane answer is rendered as a state list, or the state answer ignores the requested lane. In either case, the interrupted set for lane `L` is not returned.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/lifecycle/navigate.py:_next_text

chunk_findings.detail: `test_state_interrupted_lists_expired_running_only` asserts that after both leases are expired, `--state running` still lists `{"A", "B"}` while `--state interrupted` also lists them. The intent is to let a lane get “exactly the running or interrupted set” machine-readably, and the earlier test is named `test_state_running_lists_live_claims_not_ready`, so a script using `--state running` as the live-running set will get stale, lease-expired items and may skip work that is actually available/interrupted.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_next.py:79-80

chunk_findings.detail: The state listing does not use a consistent item identifier: `--state ready`, `--state running`, and `--state interrupted` rows are checked using `r["id"]` (lines 37, 56, 77), but `--state blocked` rows are required to have `r["item"]` and the test asserts `all("item" in r ...)`. Given `ddflow --json next --state blocked`, a script that uniformly enumerates ids with `r["id"]` will raise `KeyError: 'id'`, defeating the stated machine-readable listing goal.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_next.py:46-48

chunk_findings.detail: `_split_state` parses tags by splitting on `" --tag "` but uses `maxsplit=1` incorrectly for subsequent tags: `rest.split(" --tag ")[1:]` returns only the text *after* the first occurrence of `" --tag "` (split into one element or multiple depending on string structure), which drops any tags that appear before others or truncates the tag extraction when multiple tags are present. For example, given `rest = "running --tag tag1 --tag tag2"`, `rest.split(" --tag ")[1:]` produces `['tag1 --tag tag2']` as a single tuple element instead of `('tag1', 'tag2')`, corrupting the tag reconstruction in the output caps.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:159

chunk_findings.detail: The diff removes the `exclusive="purpose"` guard from both `state` and `lane`, so `ddflow next --lane L --state interrupted` is no longer rejected, but the renderer now handles any non-empty `lane` before `state` and has no combined lane/state path. For that input, `_next_text` enters the lane branch and ignores `--state interrupted`; if the command still produces the state-list payload selected by the previous state-first path (the handler is not changed in this diff), the lane branch raises `KeyError: 'lane'` when indexing `d['lane']`. If instead the handler returns lane data, the requested machine-readable interrupted list is silently omitted, defeating the stated `--state` listing goal.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/lifecycle/navigate.py:_next_text

chunk_findings.detail: The new `--state` handling is not combined with the existing `--lane` handling. `_next` returns the lane answer before reaching the new `if state:` block, while `_next_text` now checks `a.get("state")` before `a.get("lane")`. Given an accepted call such as `ddflow next --lane L --state running` (or MCP `ddflow_next(lane="L", state="running")`), the lane branch drops the state filter, but the text renderer still takes the state branch and calls `_state_text` on a lane answer. The result is that the requested running list for lane `L` is not produced; the flags are silently mishandled unless they are combined or explicitly rejected.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/lifecycle/navigate.py:_next/_next_text

chunk_findings.detail: The test configures `output.max_rows` to 5 and creates 12 blocked items, but it never asserts that the returned `items` list is actually truncated to 5 rows. It only checks metadata (`count`, `truncated.lists.items`, and the next-page cursor) and discards the returned `_items`. Therefore, an implementation of `next --state blocked` that returns all 12 rows while still setting the truncation metadata and cursor would pass this test, despite violating the paging cap that the test is supposed to verify.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_next.py:test_state_is_paged_and_footer_names_the_state

chunk_findings.detail: The state next-page token is built from `state`, `kind`, `phase`, and `phase_only`, but the answer being capped is `_state_answer(out, state, phase, tags)`, so `tags` is part of the current state selection while the cursor omits it. Given `ddflow next --state blocked --tag urgent --max-rows 5` with more than five blocked items tagged `urgent`, the first page is filtered by `urgent`, but the generated next-page command is only `ddflow next --state blocked` (plus any non-default kind/phase/phase-only flags). Page 2 is therefore recomputed without the `urgent` tag and can return non-urgent blocked items or skip the remaining urgent blocked items.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/lifecycle/navigate.py:_next / _state_token

chunk_findings.detail: The new tag round-trip treats tag values as bare command-string tokens. `_state_token` appends ` --tag {t}` without quoting, and the MCP next-page argument is built with `t_args.append("tag=" + ",".join(tags))`, then joined into a space-separated command string. Given `ddflow next --state blocked --tag "urgent task" --max-rows 5` and more than five blocked items tagged `urgent task`, the first page is filtered correctly, but the generated MCP next-page command is tokenized as `tag=urgent` plus a stray `task` argument (and a tag containing a comma is likewise split into two tags). The CLI branch quotes each tag with `shlex.quote(t)`, so the two next-page commands are not equivalent for the same tag value; the second page can be filtered by the wrong tag.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/output_caps.py:_split_state

chunk_findings.detail: Removing `exclusive="purpose"` from both `state` and `lane` makes `ddflow next --state interrupted --lane lane-1` an accepted invocation, but the new `_next_text` takes the `lane` branch whenever `a.get("lane")` is truthy and never reaches `_state_text`. Thus the requested state list is not produced: the command either returns a lane-answer/claim line while silently ignoring `--state`, or, if the command path returns the state-list payload for `--state`, the lane renderer attempts `d['item']`/`d['note']` on that payload and fails or emits a bogus claim command. Because the same `COMMANDS` params drive the MCP `ddflow_next` tool, the MCP path accepts the same ambiguous combination.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/lifecycle/navigate.py:_next_text (and the removed `exclusive="purpose"` on the `state`/`lane` params)
